source.title: Understanding Batch Normalization
source.authors: Johan Bjorck; C. Gomes; B. Selman; K. Weinberger

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares training and test accuracy for normalized and unnormalized ResNet-110 models under different learning rates, testing how a training condition affects generalization. It does not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The main comparison varies batch normalization and learning rate on CIFAR-10. Batch size is fixed at 128; results cited from other work are not extracted as this study's findings.
record.test_reason: The study tests batch normalization and learning rate, not any listed claim version. Batch size stays at 128, and neither magnitude-aware sharpness nor its association with generalization gaps is measured. Its discussion of large batches and sharp minima relies on prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that BN's benefits are mainly mediated by larger learning rates, which accelerate convergence and improve generalization. They argue that stronger implicit regularization explains the accuracy benefit; avoidance of sharp minima is a proposed explanation rather than a measured result.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the standard CIFAR-10 ResNet-110 training setup with SGD, momentum, weight decay, and augmentation, while varying batch normalization and learning rate rather than testing the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initial learning rate and batch-normalization placement change convergence and reported generalization; learning rate 0.1 performs better than 0.0001 in the BN model, while the unnormalized model requires 0.0001 to converge.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 ResNet-110, BN and unnormalized networks have comparable test accuracy at learning rate 0.0001. BN permits higher learning rates, which yield higher accuracy and smaller train-test gaps despite shorter training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this setup, much of BN's generalization benefit is mediated by the larger learning rates it enables.

fits_no_version.finding: BN only after the last residual block permits learning rate 0.03 and reaches 90.1% test accuracy after 330 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalizing only the final residual-block output recovers a substantial portion of BN's accuracy improvement in this setup.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code can be obtained upon request and that source code would be made public later.
record.problems: The main train-test comparisons are described qualitatively in the text, with exact accuracies available only in figures. The experiment uses one architecture and dataset; no batch-size sweep is performed.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for cited prior-work results or figure-only activation, gradient, and initialization analyses, which do not measure the train-test generalization gap named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the natural-versus-random held-out accuracy comparison.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large-versus-small batch performance under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations; batch size is fixed at 128.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, underfitting, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions because none of the rows measures their named effects. This does not dispute the reported BN and learning-rate findings. Appendix K's normalization comparisons also concern no listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-versus-random label comparison.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch test.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of generalization measures.

rows.subject: 110-layer Resnet without BN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with the best initial learning rate selected from the stated set; without batch normalization, convergence required initial learning rate 0.0001 and roughly 2400 epochs.
rows.measure: Test accuracy relative to the BN counterpart and train-test gap
rows.baseline: 110-layer Resnet with BN at initial learning rate 0.1: test accuracy higher and train-test gap smaller
rows.value: Does not attain the accuracy of its normalized counterpart; at matched learning rates, testing accuracies are comparable. Exact values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over five runs; standard deviation shown as shaded region.
rows.note: Text describes the comparison; exact plotted accuracies are not stated.
rows.check: No listed version is measured. The row combines two comparisons: unnormalized training underperforms BN at learning rate 0.1, but matches BN at 0.0001. These should be separate comparisons if retained.

rows.subject: 110-layer Resnet with BN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with initial learning rate 0.1 and the stated learning-rate schedule.
rows.baseline: BN network at initial learning rate 0.0001: test accuracy comparable to the unnormalized network at that learning rate; train-test gap larger than for BN at 0.1
rows.value: Higher test accuracy and smaller train-test gap than the low-learning-rate BN condition; exact values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over five runs; standard deviation shown as shaded region.
rows.note: The authors attribute most of BN's generalization benefit in this experiment to the higher learning rate it enables.
rows.check: The higher accuracy and smaller gap are reported, but they concern learning rate and BN, not a listed version. Training duration also varies with learning rate.

rows.subject: 110-layer Resnet with BN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with initial learning rate 0.003.
rows.baseline: Initial learning rate 0.1: higher test accuracy; initial learning rate 0.0001: lower test accuracy
rows.value: Results in between these extremes; exact value is figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over five runs; standard deviation shown as shaded region.
rows.note: The text gives the relative ordering, not exact accuracy values.
rows.check: Intermediate accuracy is not partial evidence for any listed version. This condition uses 1320 epochs, compared with approximately 2400 for learning rate 0.0001 and 165 for 0.1.

rows.subject: 110-layer Resnet with BN only at the last layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch normalization only after the last residual block and before average pooling.
rows.note: The text says this captures two-thirds of the overall BN improvement, but gives no explicit baseline accuracy here.
rows.check: The 90.1% test accuracy is correctly reported but measures no listed version. Appendix E specifies learning rate 0.03 and 330 epochs. Although no numerical baseline is supplied here, Section 4 says this captures about two-thirds of the overall BN improvement.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
